The flat path adds exactly; the two differ only past that bound

def ledger.era.rules.ShelleyUtxow.valida.note: the reference's predicate generic in its era over the reference's classes, the failing key witnesses' keys in their set's order as the reference lists them, the bootstrap witnesses' in the order of bootAddrTxWits, a sequence the decoder keeps in the reference's set order (Ord BootstrapWitness, by address root); the signature checks are the node's Verdicts, given as an argument, and a check that gives no verdict is a provider defect (Left), as in the flat check. The flat check lists the failing keys as they arrived, a difference in the refusal's content tracked on #796 (https://github.com/KD5UJC-XYZ/scarab/issues/796#issuecomment-6923378038); it reports the node's flat UtxowFailure, so its verdict is compared with the flat rule's

glue.reason: the state layout of each reference build Scarab can follow, and the defect of a build whose layout is not implemented yet, which the node's setup refuses before any rule runs (#1002, stage 0); the reference is one build and has no counterpart

the conversions between the parameters the node keeps (the flat `ProtocolParams`, the decoded `ConwayParamUpdate` and the flat voting thresholds) and the era's record; the reference keeps the record itself and has no counterpart (#85)
companion objects that only hold an era's instances, constructors or the Scala `Ordering` of a type whose order the reference derives

Scala machinery with no counterpart: the probe and invariant wrapper that let a match type tell `Identity` from `StrictMaybe`, the names of the parameter groups' singleton types, constants checked when compiled, accessors of opaque types, and the checked constructors' typed refusals
Scala names for `Identity` (base's `Data.Functor.Identity`) and `StrictMaybe` (strict-containers' `Data.Maybe.Strict`), which are outside cardano-ledger; Scala's `Option` is strict
the reading of the outputs the node keeps as an era's UTxO, refused only for an output a damaged store holds; the reference keeps the UTxO at its era's type and has no counterpart (#85)

the era-typed predicates' adapters to the node's flat failure types (UtxoFailure under PredicateFailure, and Network as the wire value they carry), until each era's failures are named (§3.4 of docs/design/era-typed-transactions.md), and the objects that stand for the reference's Rules/Utxo modules

how an output holds its reference script: by its hash and tree, without the bytes a script read from them keeps, which the output re-reads from its own encoding (#998); the reference's output holds the script whole, so this representation has no counterpart

objects that stand for the reference's modules of functions (`State/UTxO.hs`, `Shelley/UTxO.hs`, `Mary/UTxO.hs`, `Babbage/UTxO.hs`, `Alonzo/Tx.hs`), which Scala needs to hold top-level functions under a name

the conversions between Dijkstra's record and the parameters the node keeps (the flat `ProtocolParams`) and the decoded `DijkstraParamUpdate`; the reference keeps the record itself and has no counterpart (#85)

the era-typed UTXOW predicates' adapter to the node's flat failure type (UtxowFailure under PredicateFailure), until each era's failures are named (§3.4 of docs/design/era-typed-transactions.md), and the objects that stand for the reference's Rules/Utxow modules
the companions of the script integrity's types, holding their equality and the Scala Ordering of a language view, whose order the reference derives
the companions of the script integrity's types and of the era's versions, holding their instances, their equality and the Scala Ordering of a language view, whose order the reference derives
